newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INTERVIEW-Enerco sees higher profit, capex.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Enerco sees higher profit, capex.

text.p: The chief executive of New Zealand gas distributor and retailer Enerco New Zealand Ltd, Kevin Johnson, said on Friday he expected the company to post an increased profit in the current 1997/98 year.

In an interview with Reuters after the company earlier reported a jump in net profit for the year to March 31 to NZ$18.9 million, Johnson said the group planned to review its balance sheet structure around the middle of this year.
He also said Enerco planned to embark on a $60 million capital expenditure programme.

"We think that the profit will continue to increase," Johnson said. "We are not specifically disclosing a forecast profit because there are a number of changes occurring in the market place," he said.
Among the changes he highlighted was a decline in economic activity, which was starting to have an impact on Enerco's industrial base. "That's a concern," he said.
There was also increased competition. "We are faring quite well in the competitive environment, but I'm sure it will hot up over the next year or so," he said.
Johnson said he expected the company's efficiency drive to start to bear fruit towards the end of the year.

The NZ$60 million capital expenditure programme would cover a new information technology (IT) system for the entire company, which is in effect an amalgam of several small gas companies with their own systems.
It would also go towards mains expansion, the North Harbour pipeline (NZ$10 million) in Auckland and increased exploration on the East Coast ($2.5-3.0 million).
The programme would involve some extra borrowings.
Johnson said that while the industrial sector was feeling the pinch, restructuring had its advantages.
Heinz-Watties' decision to close its Gisborne plant and shift to nearby Hastings was a positive for Enerco, which services the former but not the latter.

Mains expansion would be somewhat less this year, and the focus would be on connecting customers to the network to ensure maximum utilisation. Johnson said he expected the connection rate in the current year to March to be similar to last year's of around 11,600.
Enerco is 69 percent-owned by Christchurch-based SouthPower.
The company's share price traded today at NZ$5.85, unchanged from Thursday's close.
